error.signature: AI tells someone in Italy they must download an 'IT-Alert' app to receive earthquake, volcanic, dam-collapse, or industrial-accident emergency alerts, or assumes every future IT-Alert risk category will stay app-free
error.regex: (it-alert app|italy earthquake alert app|download.*it.?alert|italy disaster warning app|it-alert.*app)

verdict.summary: IT-Alert, Italy's national public warning system run by the Dipartimento della Protezione Civile, delivers alerts via cell-broadcast technology automatically to any powered-on phone in the affected area - no app download or registration is required. It is operational for nuclear/radiological emergencies, major industrial accidents, large-dam collapse, and volcanic activity at Campi Flegrei, Vesuvius, and Vulcano; tsunami and Stromboli volcanic-activity alerts remain in an extended experimental phase through 31 December 2026 under the Direttiva Ministro PCPM of 12 February 2026. That same directive changes the plan specifically for intense-precipitation (flash-flood) alerts: cell broadcast is being dropped for that one risk type in favor of a dedicated app, required to become operational within 12 months of the directive's publication (by roughly May 2027) - so the 'no app needed' answer will stop being universally true once that app launches.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone in Italy they need to install a specific 'IT-Alert' app to receive official emergency alerts
dead_ends.why_fails: Dipartimento della Protezione Civile's own explainer states IT-Alert messages reach any powered-on mobile device in the affected area via cell-broadcast technology built into the mobile network; there is no app to install or account to register for the risk categories covered so far (nuclear/radiological, industrial accident, dam collapse, and the operational Campi Flegrei/Vesuvius/Vulcano volcanic risk).
dead_ends.condition: Nuclear, industrial-accident, dam-collapse, or Campi Flegrei/Vesuvius/Vulcano volcanic risk
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Italy's alert system works like some other countries' app-based warning systems.

dead_ends.action: Assume the 'no app needed' answer will keep applying to every future IT-Alert risk category, including intense-precipitation/flash-flood warnings
dead_ends.why_fails: The Direttiva Ministro PCPM of 12 February 2026 explicitly abandons cell broadcast for the intense-precipitation risk category specifically, citing strong local variability of weather events and the difficulty of setting uniform regional thresholds, and instead mandates a dedicated app be made operational within 12 months of the directive's publication (i.e., by roughly May 2027).
dead_ends.condition: Intense-precipitation/flash-flood risk specifically, once that app launches
dead_ends.common_misconception: That IT-Alert's delivery mechanism is uniform across every hazard type and will stay cell-broadcast-only indefinitely.

workarounds.action: Confirm the phone's built-in emergency/wireless alert setting is enabled (most modern smartphones ship with it on); no separate download is needed for the currently operational or experimental risk categories
workarounds.condition: General public in Italy, current operational and experimental risk categories

workarounds.action: For intense-precipitation/flash-flood risk once the mandated app becomes operational, check protezionecivile.gov.it for the official rollout rather than assuming cell-broadcast coverage extends to that hazard
workarounds.condition: Intense-precipitation/flash-flood risk, after the app launches

frequently_confused_with.distinction: That canon covers which number to dial for help during an emergency (112); this one covers how IT-Alert push warnings reach you before or during a hazard (automatic cell broadcast, and soon a dedicated app for one specific risk).
